To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stroke induces a complex immune response in the brain that is characterized by a temporal pattern of accumulation and spatial distribution of immune cells in the brain.

cerebral immune cell accumulation is a dynamic process that starts within hours after stroke and peaks within 3 days, that the accumulation is heterogeneous in the infarct core and the peri-infarct area, and that the accumulation of immune cells is associated with neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.

stroke-induced accumulation of leukocytes in the brain is spatially restricted and temporally dynamic, with the greatest accumulation in the subventricular zone, and that the accumulation is mediated by the chemokine CX3CL1 and its receptor CX3CR1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal and spatial dynamics of immune cell accumulation in the ischemic hemisphere after stroke.
the role of immune cells in the pathophysiology of ischemic stroke.
the development of a novel, non-invasive, and quantitative technique for the detection and characterization of the cerebral immune cell accumulation following ischemic brain injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune cells of stroke patients are not only recruited to the brain, but also to the periphery.
the role of the immune response in ischemic stroke is complex, with a multitude of factors influencing the outcome.
there is no evidence to support the use of statins in the acute phase of stroke.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal and spatial dynamics of immune cells in stroke are more complicated than previously thought.
the temporal and spatial dynamics of immune cell accumulation in the brain following stroke have not been fully elucidated.
the accumulation of immune cells in the ischemic brain is a dynamic process that is initiated by the ischemic injury and is regulated in a spatial and temporal manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal and spatial dynamics of immune cells are important for the understanding of the pathophysiology of stroke.
there is no single stroke biomarker.

the brain has the capacity to mount an immune response to injury and that the immune response to stroke is not a static phenomenon, but rather a dynamic process that changes over time and across brain regions.
